title: Reorder Buffer
constraints: 8 entries in a circular buffer. Allocation happens at the tail (tags 0, 1, …, 7, 0, …) and commit at the head, strictly in order.

Each rising edge, using the state **before** the edge: (1) if the head entry is valid and done, commit it (`commit_valid = 1` with its rd and data, pop the head); (2) `complete_valid` marks entry `complete_tag` done and stores `complete_data`; (3) `alloc_valid` allocates the tail entry if the ROB was not full (`count < 8` before the edge): `alloc_ok = 1`, `alloc_tag` = that entry.

A completion takes effect for commit at the earliest on the next edge. `count` = number of valid entries. All outputs registered. Don't-care fields: `alloc_tag` when not ok, `commit_rd`/`commit_data` when not committing.
Synchronous reset empties the ROB. Must be synthesizable.
hints: Per entry: valid, done, rd, data. Plus head, tail and count registers.
Compute `commit = valid[head] && done[head]` from the current state, then do all three updates in one clocked block.

examples.title: out-of-order completion
examples.input: complete tag 2, then tag 0, then tag 1
examples.expected: commits: 0, then 1 and 2 on consecutive edges (in order)
